messages.content:
You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: By which date must the Commission adopt the delegated acts provided for in Article 6(11) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (common methodology for the data Member States must provide)?

Passages:
[0] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 45(2) — rank: law
Article 45 Exercise of the delegation. 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 18(3) and Article 26(10) shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 12 June 2023.

[1] REG, Art. 47(2) — rank: law — corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 3: '13 July 2023' now reads '19 July 2023')
Article 47 Exercise of the delegation. 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Articles 6(2), 6(11) and 7(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 19 July 2023. The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.

[2] eu-reg-2016-425, Art. 43(2) — rank: law
Article 43 Exercise of the delegation. 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 42 shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 21 April 2018. The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period. It is of particular importance that the Commission follow its usual practice and carry out consultations with experts, including Member States' experts, before adopting those delegated acts.

[3] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 97(2) — rank: law
Article 97 Exercise of the delegation. 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 6(6) and (7), Article 7(1) and (3), Article 11(3), Article 43(5) and (6), Article 47(5), Article 51(3), Article 52(4) and Article 53(5) and (6) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 1 August 2024. The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.

[4] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 18(3) — rank: law
Article 18 Specific traceability requirements for certain products, categories or groups of products. 3. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 45 to supplement this Regulation by: (a) determining the products, categories or groups of products or components likely to present a serious risk to the health and safety of consumers as referred to in paragraph 1; the Commission shall state in the delegated acts concerned whether it has used the risk analysis methodology provided for in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/417 ( 30 ) or, if that methodology is not appropriate for the product concerned, it shall give a detailed description of the methodology used; (b) specifying the type of data which economic operators are to collect and store by means of the system of traceability referred to in paragraph 2; (c) specifying the modalities to display and to access data, including placement of a data carrier on the product, its packaging or accompanying documents as referred to in paragraph 2; (d) specifying the actors that shall have access to the data as referred to in point (b) and to what data they shall have access, including consumers, economic operators, providers of online marketplaces, competent national authorities, the Commission, and public interest organisations, or any organisation acting on their behalf.

[5] eu-dir-2012-18, Art. 21(5) — rank: law
Article 21 Information system and exchanges. 5. The Commission shall, by 1 January 2015, adopt implementing acts to establish the formats for communicating the information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article from Member States and the relevant databases referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 27(2).

[6] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 53(5) — rank: law
Article 53 Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models. 5. For the purpose of facilitating compliance with Annex XI, in particular points 2 (d) and (e) thereof, the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies with a view to allowing for comparable and verifiable documentation.

[7] eu-dir-2014-68, Art. 49(1) — rank: law
Article 49 Transposition. 1. Member States shall adopt and publish, by 28 February 2015, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 13. They shall forthwith communicate the text of those measures to the Commission. They shall apply those measures from 1 June 2015. When Member States adopt those measures, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or be accompanied by such reference on the occasion of their official publication. They shall also include a statement that references in existing laws, regulations and administrative provisions to Article 9 of Directive 97/23/EC shall be construed as references to Article 13 of this Directive. Member States shall determine how such reference is to be made and how that statement is to be formulated.

[8] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 53(6) — rank: law
Article 53 Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models. 6. The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97(2) to amend Annexes XI and XII in light of evolving technological developments.

[9] REG, Art. 6(11) — rank: law
Article 6 Categories of machinery and related products listed in Annex I subject to relevant conformity assessment procedures. 11. If necessary after the Commission report referred to in Article 53(3), the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 47 to supplement paragraph 5 of this Article by specifying the obligations of Member States to provide data and information required pursuant to this Article through the establishment of a common methodology concerning the data and information to be collected, including the methods for their collection and compilation, and the procedures for their transmission, as well as the relevant definitions, in order to ensure that sufficient and comparable data is available for the Commission to carry out the assessment referred to in paragraph 4.

[10] eu-dir-2014-35, Art. 26(1) — rank: law
Article 26 Transposition. 1. Member States shall adopt and publish, by 19 April 2016, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 2, the first paragraph of Article 3, Article 4, Articles 6 to 12, Article 13(1), Articles 14 to 25 and Annexes II, III and IV. They shall forthwith communicate the text of those measures to the Commission. They shall apply those measures from 20 April 2016. When Member States adopt those measures, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or be accompanied by such a reference on the occasion of their official publication. They shall also include a statement that references in existing laws, regulations and administrative provisions to the Directive repealed by this Directive shall be construed as references to this Directive. Member States shall determine how such reference is to be made and how that statement is to be formulated.

[11] eu-dir-2010-75, Art. 76(1) — rank: law
Article 76 Exercise of the delegation. 1. The power to adopt the delegated acts referred to in Article 48(5) and Article 74 shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of 5 years from 6 January 2011. The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegated power at the latest 6 months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation of power shall be automatically extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council revokes it in accordance with Article 77.

response.text: {"reasoning": "Article 6(11) delegated acts are governed by Article 47 of the Regulation, per passage 9. Passage 1 (corrected by the corrigendum, so '19 July 2023' is the valid start date) confirms the power under Article 6(11) is conferred for five years from 19 July 2023, so the period ends on 19 July 2028. The passage sets the period of delegated power and does not use the words 'by which date must adopt', so this is the end of the delegation period, not a separate adoption deadline.", "kind": "date", "value": "2028-07-19", "text": "Under Article 47(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the Commission's power to adopt the Article 6(11) delegated acts runs for five years from 19 July 2023, so the period ends on 19 July 2028 (the corrigendum corrected the start date from 13 July 2023).", "evidence": [{"passage": 1, "quote": "The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Articles 6(2), 6(11) and 7(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 19 July 2023."}]}
